evidence.note: Created a 7-task decomposition covering the real subsystems (build/CLI, shims, plugin+resolution, App Router, Pages Router, middleware/config, integration tests) in a sensible dependency-aware order — resolution/plugin before routers, setup first — rather than one undifferentiated push. But tasks largely mirror the requirement bullets and only the final task carries an explicit test gate.
TaskUpdate calls move milestones between in_progress/completed, showing the agent maintained and tracked its milestone plan rather than abandoning it.

End-to-end verification (pack, fixture setup, dev boot, route fetch, catch-all/params debug, re-test) happens only after most subsystems were written — a layered/big-bang integration rather than establishing a minimal one-route vertical slice early to gate later work.

reasoning: The agent produced a genuine subsystem decomposition with a sensible, partly dependency-aware sequence (setup → plugin/resolution → routers → middleware → integration), and tracked milestone state via task updates, which clears anchor 5. It edges toward 6 because of the explicit ordering that puts resolution/plugin before routing. It falls short of anchor 8 because milestones lack per-milestone done-criteria tied to specific fixtures/tests (only the final task references the suite), the plan closely mirrors the requirement bullets, and no minimal end-to-end vertical slice was sequenced before layering all features — integration/testing was deferred to the end rather than gating progress incrementally.
